newsitem.title: UK: EMU expectations stable in latest week - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: EMU expectations stable in latest week - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European monetary union in 1999 changed little last week, according to financial prices monitored by JP Morgan.

Prices indicated that the probability assumed by the market of Spain and Britain joining Germany and France in the first wave of EMU edged up during the week, according to the U.S. investment firm's "EMU calculator".

The probability of Spain joining in 1999 rose by one point to 68 percent, while that of Britain ticked up by two points to 36 percent. The expectation for Britain, however, was still below the 44 percent seen a month ago.
Italy's edged down one point to 51 percent.
The calculator showed the readings for France and Belgium remained at 100 percent.
JP Morgan point out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of between three and five points.
Elsewhere, the probability of Ireland joining the first wave edged down one point to 58 percent, which was down from the 73 seen a month ago.
The reading for Denmark was 47 percent, which was down seven points from last week but almost the same as the 48 seen a month ago.
Sweden was up one point at 57 percent, while Finland was down two at 74. The probability for Portugal was unchanged at 72 percent.
JP Morgan's EMU calculator is derived from the interest rate swaps market.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU were not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
